title: Body and health — when your head does the hurting
goal: Say what hurts, talk at the pharmacy and the doctor's office — and understand a sentence pattern that makes the body part the subject.
bekal: name body parts and the most common complaints
use the pattern سرم درد می‌کند, which works differently from English
buy medicine and explain how you feel to a doctor

dialogs.title: گفتگو — در داروخانه
dialogs.intro: The morning after a long bus ride. Budi walks into a pharmacy looking worn out.

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: سلام. حالم خوب نیست. سرم خیلی درد می‌کند.
lines.baca: salâm. hâlam khub nist. saram kheyli dard mikonad.
lines.id: Hello. I don't feel well. I have a bad headache.
lines.literal: hello. state-my good is-not. head-my very pain does-it.

lines.speaker: داروساز:
lines.id: Do you have a fever too?

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: فکر می‌کنم بله. دیشب سرما خوردم.
lines.baca: fekr mikonam bale. dishab sarmâ khordam.
lines.id: I think so. I caught a cold last night.
lines.literal: thought do-I yes. last-night cold ate-I.

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: بله، و سرفه می‌کنم. دیشب اصلاً نخوابیدم.
lines.baca: bale, va sorfe mikonam. dishab aslan nakhâbidam.
lines.id: Yes, and I'm coughing. I didn't sleep at all last night.
lines.literal: yes, and cough do-I. last-night at-all not-slept-I.

lines.speaker: داروساز:
lines.text: این قرص را روزی سه بار بعد از غذا بخورید.
lines.baca: in ghors râ ruzi se bâr ba'd az ghazâ bekhorid.
lines.id: Take these tablets three times a day after meals.
lines.literal: this tablet [obj] per-day three time after from food eat-you.

lines.speaker: داروساز:
lines.text: پنج روز. و این شربت برایِ گلویتان.
lines.baca: panj ruz. va in sharbat barâye galuyetân.
lines.id: Five days. And this syrup is for your throat.
lines.literal: five day. and this syrup for-of throat-your.

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.id: Do I need to see a doctor too?

lines.speaker: داروساز:
lines.text: اگر تا سه روزِ دیگر بهتر نشدید، بله.
lines.baca: agar tâ se ruz-e digar behtar nashodid, bale.
lines.id: If you're not better in three days, yes.
lines.literal: if up-to three day-of other better not-become-you, yes.

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.id: Thank you. How much is it all?

lines.speaker: داروساز:
lines.text: هشتاد هزار تومان. زود خوب شوید!
lines.baca: hashtâd hezâr tomân. zud khub shavid!
lines.id: Eighty thousand tomans. Get well soon!
lines.literal: eighty thousand toman. quickly good become-you!

notes: ⚠️ **The sentence سرم درد می‌کند literally means "my head does pain" — the body part is the subject, not the person.** English also says "my head hurts" with the head as subject; Persian just packages the verb as درد می‌کند ("does pain"). Learn it as one unit. The pattern works for the whole body: دستم درد می‌کند، پایم درد می‌کند، دندانم درد می‌کند.
**"I don't feel well" = حالم خوب نیست**, literally "my state isn't good". The most useful opening line at a pharmacy or doctor's office. Its opposite: حالم بهتر است ("I feel better").
**"Three times a day" = روزی سه بار.** The ـی on روز again means "per", just like کیلویی in unit 7. هفته‌ای دو بار ("twice a week"), سالی یک بار ("once a year").

**"Get well soon" = زود خوب شوید**, literally "quickly become good". Said by pharmacists, doctors, friends, and anyone who knows you're sick. Its relatives: انشاءالله زود خوب می‌شوید and خدا شفا بدهد.
**"I have to go" = باید بروم.** Notice the verb form after باید: **بروم**, not می‌روم. This is the التزامی form, and all of unit 18 is devoted to it. For now, memorize the pair: باید + بـ.
**Spoken forms:** حالم خوب نیست (unchanged), سرم درد می‌کنه (*saram dard mikone*), تب دارین؟ (*tab dârin?*), زود خوب شین! (*zud khub shin!*).

grammars.title: The complaint pattern: درد می‌کند
body: To say which body part hurts, the pattern is: **body part + possessive ending + درد می‌کند**. The body part is the subject, so the verb is always in the او form.
after: **The past forms:** درد می‌کرد ("it was hurting") or درد گرفت ("it started hurting").
**To ask:** کجایتان درد می‌کند؟ (*kojâyetân dard mikonad?*, "where does it hurt?"). This is the first thing a doctor will say to you.

The same pattern is used for a few other states: **سردم است** ("I'm cold", literally "my cold is"), **گرمم است** ("I'm hot"), **خوابم می‌آید** ("I'm sleepy", literally "my sleep comes"), **حالم بد است** ("I feel unwell").

grammars.title: Parts of the body
after: ⚠️ Look at **بدن** (*badan*, "body") — an Arabic loanword. Several other body and medical words came from Arabic too: **قلب** ("heart"), **صورت** ("face"), and **معده** ("stomach").

⚠️ **The word دل means both "belly" and "heart" (feelings).** دلم درد می‌کند = "my stomach hurts". دلم تنگ است = "I miss (someone)". Context tells them apart — much as English "heart" can be an organ or a feeling.

grammars.title: Complaints and conditions
after: For allergies: **به ... حساسیت دارم** (*be ... hassâsiyat dâram*). به بادام‌زمینی حساسیت دارم ("I'm allergic to peanuts"). If you do have an allergy, memorize this sentence before you leave home.

blocks.text: ⚠️ **Iranian pharmacies do more than pharmacies in many other countries.** For minor complaints — a cold, a headache, an upset stomach — the pharmacist (داروساز) will listen, ask questions, and give you medicine without a doctor's prescription. For anything more serious, they'll send you to a doctor. This saves a lot of time and money, and that's why this unit's dialog takes place at a pharmacy, not a hospital.

blocks.title: Emergency numbers and phrases
items: Ambulance: **۱۱۵ اورژانس** · Police: **۱۱۰ پلیس** · Fire: **۱۲۵ آتش‌نشانی**.
*komak!* **کمک!** — "Help!" · *âmbulâns khabar konid!* **آمبولانس خبر کنید!** — "Call an ambulance!" · *hâlash bad ast* **حالش بد است** — "He/She is in a bad way".
**Your embassy** (for Budi: **سفارتِ اندونزی در تهران**) — if you lose your passport or get into serious trouble, the sentence is: پاسپورتم را گم کرده‌ام، باید به سفارت بروم.

blocks.title: Six sentences for when you're sick in Iran
items: "I don't feel well." — حالم خوب نیست.
"My head / stomach / throat hurts." — سرم / دلم / گلویم درد می‌کند.
"I have a fever." — تب دارم.
"I'm allergic to ..." — به ... حساسیت دارم.
"Where is the nearest pharmacy?" — نزدیک‌ترین داروخانه کجاست؟
"I need a doctor." — دکتر لازم دارم. These six sentences are worth memorizing before you leave, not after you arrive.
I don't feel well.
My head hurts.
I have a fever.
I caught a cold last night.
Where is the nearest pharmacy?
